notes.summary: Bounded numerical Cartier comparison on all excellent reductions: actual curve-nef model potentials have exactly the primary-ideal uniform closure. A finite-algebra correction handles nonnormal sections and nonminimal valuation supports; no unbounded psh recovery is claimed.
notes.detailedSummary: For every positive-dimensional excellent reduced Noetherian local ring and primary normalized semivaluation section, construct a model core on primary-ideal blowups from negative real sums of effective exceptional integral Cartier divisors, with positivity tested on contracted integral proper curves. Prove finite continuous evaluation, directed domination, numerical pullback independence, corrected descent of generated sections, rational ample perturbation and uniform ideal approximation. Conversely primary ideals give globally generated nef models. Compare the dossier's unclosed finite real ideal cone explicitly, retaining the distinction between it and its uniform closure. Prove the primary-gauge cocycle and reduction convention. This is a bounded continuous theorem under precisely stated ordinary projective background, not the complete original P12.2 solution.
notes.text:
Claim and definitions. Let (R,m) be a positive-dimensional excellent reduced Noetherian local ring, U its punctured spectrum, and a an m-primary ideal. V_a consists of nonnegative real semivaluations v with v(a)=1, including nonminimal supports. Let I_a={0} union {-v(I)/k: I m-primary, k a positive integer}. On Y=Bl_b Spec(R), b primary, put b O_Y=O_Y(-E_b). A geometric core potential is v(D), where D=-sum a_j B_j, the coefficients a_j are nonnegative real numbers, B_j are effective exceptional integral Cartier divisors with their rational sections trivial on U, and D has nonnegative degree on every contracted integral proper curve. The negative-cone convention is explicit on nonnormal schemes. The uniform closures of this core and I_a are equal. All core values are finite, continuous and nonpositive. No normality, characteristic, residue-field, pure-dimension, algebraization, density or resolution hypothesis is imposed.

Ordinary background, with scope. Proper pushforward of coherent sheaves over Noetherian affine bases is finite and localizes. Ample invertible sheaves on projective Noetherian morphisms generate high twists of coherent sheaves. On projective schemes over an arbitrary field, numerical nef plus positive ample is ample; ampleness is open in a fixed finite real span and lifts from a closed fiber to a base neighborhood. Over a local base that neighborhood is the whole base. Nilpotent fiber thickenings do not change ampleness. Proper valuative lifting applies to arbitrary valuation rings. Excellence supplies finite normalization of reduced quotients, and one-dimensional normal local domains are DVRs. These inputs are declared with their applications checked, rather than treated as caller grants.

Boundary proof. If m^r is contained in a and a is contained in m^s, then s v(m)<=v(a)<=r v(m). All primary values are therefore positive, finite and bounded on a primary section. Semivaluation equations define a closed subset of the compact product [0,infinity]^R: extended nonnegative addition and minimum are continuous. The condition v(m)=1 is closed by finite generation. Thus V_m is compact Hausdorff, and rescaling gives the same conclusion for V_a. A one-dimensional excellent quotient obtained from a penultimate prime in a maximal chain, followed by finite normalization and a DVR localization, supplies a point. Units have value zero and the infinite locus is prime, possibly nonminimal. Nilpotents have infinite value; applying ultrametricity twice gives v(f+n)=v(f), so reduction preserves boundaries and ideal gauges. A zero-dimensional local reduction is a field and has empty centered boundary.

Models and numerical independence. Blowup charts R[b/f] embed in R_f, are reduced, and have nonzerodivisor f generating b O_Y. Every component meets U densely, and O(-E_b) is relatively ample. Bl_(bd) dominates Bl_b and Bl_d: locally, if IJ=(e) with e regular, then I(J/e)=A. In 1=sum i_l j_l/e one summand is a unit; its i_l is regular and generates I, since x/i_l=(xj_l/e)/(i_lj_l/e) belongs to A for every x in I. Both factors are therefore invertible. The projective domination maps are surjective by density of U. Pullback preserves nefness by the curve degree formula. It reflects nefness too: a closed point of the generic fiber over any downstairs contracted curve has finite residue extension; its closure is an integral proper curve dominating that curve and detects its degree. These curves lie in projective fibers over the residue field, so this works without an algebraically closed residue field. This proves independence under Cartier pullback in the directed primary-blowup system, without asserting cofinality among all projective modifications.

Finite evaluation. If p is the support of v, then p is not m. The valuation ring of K=Frac(R/p) has a unique proper lift to Y from its generic map in U. A local Cartier equation g of B at the center restricts to a nonzero K-element because it is a unit on U. Define v(B)=v_K(g). Changing g multiplies it by a local unit of the valuation ring, of value zero. This definition is additive, homogeneous and pullback-compatible and never forms infinity-minus-infinity. A minimizing finite generator of b gives a blowup chart and v(E_b)=v(b). On a finite affine cover with E_b equation e, the complement of the fiber is D(e), and g and 1/g belong to A_e. Clearing powers gives regular elements e^N g and e^N/g in A, hence -N E_b<=B<=N E_b and |v(B)|<=N v(b). Evaluation of arbitrary finite real combinations is consequently finite and uniformly bounded.

Finite-algebra correction. T=H0(Y,O_Y) is finite over R, contains R injectively by density of U, and T/R is supported at m. Choose h with m^h(T/R)=0 and c=m^(h+1), so cT is contained in m and in R. For a negative rational D' and a globally generated integral multiple kD', F_k=H0(Y,O(kD')) is a finite submodule of T generating an invertible ideal. I_k=c F_k is a downstairs ideal contained in m and is the unit ideal away from m, hence is primary. At every proper valuation lift, finite generating sections equal a local basis of value -k v(D') times coefficients generating the unit ideal. Their minimum coefficient value is zero. Thus, exactly,

v(I_k)=v(c)-k v(D'), and -v(I_k)/k=v(D')-v(c)/k.

All terms are finite, including at nonminimal supports. The actual sheaf equality is I_k O_Y=(c O_Y)O(kD'), not uncorrected equality. For arbitrary integral exceptional B, high twisting gives B-nE_b<=0 with O(B-nE_b) generated. The same formula gives v(B)=v(c)+n v(b)-v(I) for a primary I. Primary ideal evaluations are finite continuous minima, so every real model evaluation is continuous.

Uniform approximation. If D=-sum a_j B_j is numerical nef, then D-epsilon E_b is relatively ample by nef-plus-ample on the projective closed fiber and the local-base ampleness statement. Approximate coefficients by nonnegative rationals in their fixed finite span, keeping a positive rational coefficient of -E_b. Openness gives a negative rational ample D' arbitrarily close. The divisor bounds give

||v(D)-v(D')|| <= M_b(sum |a_j-a'_j|N_j+epsilon'),

where M_b=max_Va v(b). Clear denominators q and use generation of all high powers k=q l. The fixed correction c then gives total error at most the displayed perturbation error plus M_c/k, where M_c=max_Va v(c). Let both errors tend to zero. Every geometric core potential belongs to the ideal uniform closure. Conversely, -E_I/k on Bl_I is negative and globally generated, hence curve-nef: a section nonzero at the generic point of an integral proper curve has an effective zero divisor of nonnegative degree. Its value is -v(I)/k. Zero is a model too. Both inclusions prove equality of uniform closures.

Exact finite-cone comparison and gauges. At denominator kl, sums and maxima of two ideal profiles are represented by I^l J^k and I^l+J^k. Powers give rational scalars; real scalars follow uniformly. The dossier's finite-transfer cone P_a is an unclosed finite nonnegative real combination of positive ideal gauges, with ideals containing a boundary power. On a local ring these ideals are primary or unit. After reversing the sign, each finite real sum is a nef negative Cartier model on a common primary blowup. Thus -P_a lies in the geometric core. Rational approximation of its finitely many coefficients and product ideals prove that its uniform closure is exactly C^id. Equality before closure is not asserted. The uniform closures are closed convex cones stable under finite maxima. For another primary ideal d, H(v)=v/v(d) and (T u)(H(v))=u(v)/v(d). Primary bounds make T and its inverse bounded for uniform norms. Homogeneity proves the exact cocycle and carries both constructions to the new section.

Evidence and limitations. This is a mathematical proof draft under the stated ordinary background, not a computational correctness certificate. Expanded proofs are in argument.md Sections 1–6 and P12.2-paper.tex. Rerun: python3 own-tools/make_paper.py, followed by pdflatex -no-shell-escape -interaction=nonstopmode -halt-on-error -output-directory=build P12.2-paper.tex. The final standalone paper has 14 pages; initial build warnings and outputs are retained. This bounded uniform theorem does not discharge original P12.2.

notes.summary: Exact bounded product/descent for isolated finite birational discrepancy. Reduced-curve normalization is a primary conductor blowup, so numerical models already realize every finite nonpositive branch profile. A mixed-zero node model disproves uncorrected section descent and differs from the specified radial cone.
notes.detailedSummary: Using n1, prove a boundary homeomorphism and isometric product description for finite R⊂T⊂Q(R) equal to R away from the closed point. Corrected powers of synchronized branch ideals prove the converse. Reconstruct the general normalization boundary quotient, but retain the general cone-descent gap. On reduced excellent curves prove normalization belongs to the chosen primary-blowup system, realize all finite nonpositive profiles geometrically, and independently prove the principal-ideal comparison. In the isolated normalization case the bounded cone contains the dossier's raw normalization-ideal cone and equals its uniform closure. The task's radial CLD/classical cone is only a specified comparator; its unavailable analytic dependencies are not granted.
notes.text:
Use n1's bounded comparison, boundary facts and ordinary background. If R⊂T⊂Q(R) is finite and T/R is supported at the closed point, choose a primary c with cT⊂m. Every downstairs normalized semivaluation v has a unique lift: choose d∈c with v(d) finite and set w(t)=v(dt)-v(d). Independence follows from d'(dt)=d(d't); multiplication follows from (dt)(du)=d(dtu). A monic integral equation excludes w(t)<0 because its highest-degree term would be uniquely smallest. Thus w is nonnegative and extends v, without subtracting infinities. Its center is a maximal ideal above m because T/mT is finite over the residue field. Localization at that center gives a local branch semivaluation; denominators have value zero. There are finitely many centers, with clopen pieces selected by Chinese-remainder elements zero at one center and one at the others. Restriction is a continuous bijection from their compact union to the Hausdorff downstairs link, hence a homeomorphism.

The bounded cone equals the product of the local branch cones. Downstairs primary ideals extend to primary ideals on every branch. Conversely approximate each component by a rational ideal profile or zero, synchronize denominators k by taking powers, and denote the local ideals by B_i, allowing the unit ideal for zero. Contract and intersect to obtain a T-ideal H with these localizations. Each contraction contains a power of its named maximal ideal, is primary there and becomes the unit at the other centers. For M>0, I_M=c H^M⊂m⊂R is the unit off the closed point, hence downstairs primary. On branch i,

-w(I_M)/(Mk)=-w(B_i)/k-w(c)/(Mk).

The last term is uniformly bounded by a constant divided by Mk. Let M grow and improve the finite tuple of approximants. This proves surjectivity onto the product; the boundary homeomorphism proves the maximum-norm isometry. Apply this to normalization only when its discrepancy is supported at the closed point. This is function descent, not uncorrected line-bundle descent. In that isolated normalization case the bounded cone contains the dossier's raw sign-reversed normalization-ideal cone and equals its uniform closure: local finite real combinations assemble on each semilocal component using ideals primary at one center and unit at the others, then finite real sums. Such ideals contain a boundary power. Finite-component approximation proves density. No equality of unclosed cones is asserted.

General normalization boundary rule, independently reconstructed. Finite normalization S=product S_j has conductor f=(R:S), an ideal of both rings containing a regular element by denominator clearing. The identity R=S×_(S/f)R/f follows by subtracting a common residue. To lift a valuation with support p, choose a minimal component contained in p and a normalization prime above p; the quotient fraction fields give a finite extension L/K. A local domain inside L has a dominating valuation ring by Zorn. Indeed a maximal dominating local ring W must contain x or x^-1: if neither belongs, maximality gives M W[x]=W[x] and M W[x^-1]=W[x^-1]. The latter equality makes x integral, and the former then contradicts Nakayama for the finite module W[x]. Apply this to a localization of the integral closure of the downstairs valuation ring A in L. Its dominating valuation ring intersects K in A, since inverses of elements outside A lie in its maximal ideal. Polynomial relations have at least two minimal terms, so each new value has a nonzero integer multiple in the original value group. Dividing that multiple uniquely embeds the extended group in the reals. Restriction to the normalization quotient, with infinity on its support, supplies a nonnegative normalized lift.

Compactness now gives the quotient by equal restrictions. At v(f)<infinity, a finite-valued conductor element d determines the lift by w(s)=v(ds)-v(d). At v(f)=infinity, all lifts factor through S/f, and equality on R/f is exactly the remaining relation. These rules commute with primary gauges. Downstairs bounded cones pull back into fiber-constant products by ideal extension and n1. Surjectivity remains unproved for positive-dimensional conductor support: v(f) can be infinite, so no uniform correction follows. The raw normalization-ideal cone and our bounded cone both map into that product; this does not compare the two downstairs classes in general.

Curve theorem. In a one-dimensional reduced excellent local ring every normalized support is minimal. A valuation of its component field dominates a normalization DVR and is a positive multiple of its order, because every field element is a unit times a uniformizer power. Hence the boundary is the finite discrete branch set v_i=ord_i/d_i, d_i=ord_i(a)>0, including different normalization points on one irreducible component. Normalization S is semilocal Dedekind. Its conductor is invertible upstairs and primary downstairs unless R=S. Its primary blowup equals Spec S: on a chart for a conductor generator f, every s∈S satisfies s=(fs)/f∈R[conductor/f], so that chart equals S[conductor/f], interpreted in the common localized components. The upstairs blowup is the identity because the conductor is invertible. If R=S, use the DVR maximal ideal instead.

Closed branch points P_i are effective Cartier divisors and this finite model has no contracted integral curves. For every finite tuple u_i<=0, D=sum d_i u_i P_i belongs to the negative real Cartier cone, is numerical nef vacuously and evaluates to u_i. Thus the model core itself is the entire finite nonpositive orthant. Its finite-link decreasing completion is all extended nonpositive profiles by truncation max(u,-n).

The principal comparison is exact independently. If conductor orders are c_i, every vector k_i>=max(c_i,1) gives an invertible S-ideal J=product n_i^k_i contained in R. Chinese remainders select an element nonzero in each J/n_i J; Nakayama makes it generate J at every localization and therefore globally. It is regular in R, belongs to m and generates a primary ideal with those exact branch orders. A sufficiently divisible common denominator realizes any strictly negative rational profile. Their uniform closure is the finite nonpositive orthant, agreeing with n1.

Explicit node. For R=k[[x,y]]/(xy), S=k[[x]]×k[[y]], the conductor is m and Bl_m has the two disjoint normalization charts. D=-P_x is numerical nef with profile (-1,0). Yet H0(O(kD))=x^k k[[x]]×k[[y]] contains (0,1), which is not in R. Multiplying by m produces I_k=(x^(k+1),y), with profile (-1-1/k,-1/k) and uniform error 1/k. This disproves uncorrected descent and checks the correction sign. Against the task's specified radial class {0}∪[-infinity,0)^q, the numerical completed cone adds exactly the mixed-zero profiles for q>=2. No new CLD classification is claimed: original GR25/Chapter 15 dependencies are unavailable, and the radial set is a comparison specification rather than a proof grant.

Expanded proofs are in argument.md Sections 7–9 and P12.2-paper.tex. Exact diagnostics for k=1,2,3,4,8,16,32 are in evidence/exact-diagnostics.json; rerun python3 own-tools/exact_diagnostics.py. They check finite arithmetic, not exhaustive geometry. General conductor descent and unbounded psh gates remain open.

notes.summary: Frozen-source diagnostics: BdFFU Proposition 2.4(b) has a PDF-confirmed reversed retraction sign, refuted by an elementary valuation. BFJ Proposition 3.13 needs a separate zero/unit case. Neither affected statement is used as an unqualified grant.
notes.detailedSummary: Record source versions, URLs, hashes, exact LF/PDF coordinates and domain restrictions. BdFFU prints retracted ideal value greater than actual value although its proof yields the opposite; weights in coordinates x,z=x+y give actual value 2 and retracted value 1. The same page contains a concave/convex prose mismatch. BFJ's literal primary-only decreasing approximation cannot cover zero under the proper-primary convention. Immediate BFJ units and dependencies were inspected, but unavailable original principalization and multiplier-subadditivity units receive no source-PASS.
notes.text:
BFJ source: author-hosted published Valuations and Plurisubharmonic Singularities, Publ. RIMS 44 (2008), 449–494, 46 pages; URL https://sebastien.boucksom.perso.math.cnrs.fr/publis/BFJ_psh.pdf. PDF SHA-256: 26d2d8dd2546efd55a148b4ff233892e88cfeab6c34de7fa613a7ad2e543d7f8. Bound text SHA-256: 9a72054bc227fca9231feb65ec631e6b4a91e68c10307d38fa5c23d5965de93f. Its formal Sections 1–4 assume a smooth point over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero; Section 5 returns to complex analytic germs. Definition 2.1 is weak closure of ideal divisors; Proposition 2.2 is the Cartier numerical comparison; Definition 2.5 requires finite strong continuity; Definition 2.8 extends by an infimum of retractions; Proposition 3.11 uses multiplier estimates for closed-face continuity. These are distinct gates. Complete immediate units and their dependencies were inspected, not conflated into global uniform regularization. Original external principalization and usual multiplier-subadditivity units are not bound; no separate source-PASS is fabricated.

BdFFU source: author version compiled June 27, 2013, filename BdFFU-13-2706, 17 pages; URL https://sebastien.boucksom.perso.math.cnrs.fr/publis/BdFFU.pdf. PDF SHA-256: 22918838aedf3feaaf7a5581d58944dbded754fcd322a342486e8a7fb7bd6fa6. Bound text SHA-256: 34ebf6a3299a6af06bcea23bf3847e1f5da87735e3420f86dea1bce3aca8ce29. It works over C; its valuation space uses finite real function-field valuations, and its singular multiplier statements assume normal varieties. It supplies no nonnormal excellent all-semivaluation theorem.

At literal BdFFU LF 274–298, Proposition 2.4 and its complete proof, part (b) at LF 279 prints r_pi^N(nu)(a)>=nu(a), while the proof at LF 296 obtains nu(f)>=nu_w(f). PDF page 6 has the same printed sign, so this is not a text-extraction artifact. Counterexample in its permitted smooth complex setting: on A^2 take N the origin and pi its blowup. In algebraically independent coordinates x,z=x+y take monomial weights nu(x)=1, nu(z)=2. Then y=z-x has value min(2,1)=1 and nu(m)=1. The first blowup dual complex has one vertex, whose normalized retraction is ordinary order. The ideal (x+y) has actual value 2 and retracted value 1. Thus the printed 1>=2 is false. The same page, LF 291–292, calls a minimum concave and then calls the ideal minimum convex. These observations concern the bound version, not unspecified later versions or all its results.

BFJ Proposition 3.13, LF 1199–1216 and PDF page 27, printed page 475, literally states decreasing approximation by positive multiples of primary ideal profiles for every formal psh function. Under the proper m-primary convention this cannot approximate zero: every profile is strictly negative at each normalized valuation, and a decreasing sequence remains below its first negative value. A unit ideal must be permitted for zero, or zero treated separately. This obstruction uses no multiplier theorem. Our model family includes zero explicitly.

All fourteen frozen bound lengths and hashes matched. Exact application scopes, LF unit spans, dependency restrictions and recursive include coverage are in source-application-ledger.md and input-hashes.json. Typography evidence is retained in evidence/BdFFU-06.png and evidence/BFJ-21.png, evidence/BFJ-23.png, evidence/BFJ-27.png. Rerun the independent arithmetic example with python3 own-tools/exact_diagnostics.py. No supplied script, reviewer or receipt was executed or accepted as authority, and no network was used.

notes.summary: Original P12.2 remains OPEN; candidate=false. Deliver a 14-page standalone paper, complete argument, notes, scope/source/coverage ledgers and reproducible hashes. Bounded geometric progress does not recover full BFJ or the general conductor/unbounded interfaces.
notes.detailedSummary: Using n1–n3, record the exact original-scope decision. Within an explicitly conditional BFJ simple-principalization/retraction framework, prove weak-nef coefficients, closed-face continuity and convexity, and the all-semivaluation extension for the bounded numerical cone. The example -v(z_1) in dimension at least two prevents identification with the full unbounded BFJ class. General conductor cone surjectivity, unbounded positivity and extension, and analytic trace comparison remain gates; P12.3–P12.6 remain separate. Final typesetting and exact diagnostics succeeded, with initial warnings and the failed own edit retained. Execution is not mathematical certification.
notes.text:
The exact controlling original task asks for an independently geometric cone for arbitrary excellent singular or nonnormal germs, full smooth BFJ specialization, primary gauge and normalization/conductor comparison with the existing ideal cone. Its family dossier keeps envelopes, products, energy and geometric finite-map operators separate. Notes n1 and n2 prove a substantive bounded comparison on all excellent reductions and exact isolated bounded descent; they do not solve this residual.

Smooth interface, with its source gate explicit. Restrict to R=C[z_1,...,z_n]_(z) and assume the BFJ simple principalizing models and monomial retractions of its smooth framework. Original Hironaka/principalization bytes are not bound, so this interface is conditional on that framework, without a separate source-PASS. For a uniform limit u of rational primary ideal functions, its divisorial coefficients converge into the weak closed nef cone of Definition 2.1. Restrictions to closed quasimonomial faces are finite continuous and convex: negative monomial minima are maxima of affine functions. Hence Definition 2.5 is satisfied. Each primary ideal is principalized on a simple model; retraction reduces valuations and preserves its primary generator on that model. Therefore u_j(v)=inf_pi u_j(r_pi v) at every semivaluation. If ||u-u_j||<=delta_j, taking infima gives |inf_pi u(r_pi v)-u_j(v)|<=delta_j. This proves the exact Definition 2.8 extension for u, including nonzero supports. It establishes positivity and extension for a bounded continuous subcone, beyond the one-branch test.

For n>=2 the smooth formal class contains g(v)=-v(z_1). Its weak-nef divisor is the coefficientwise limit of divisors of (z_1)+m^N; its closed quasimonomial face restrictions are finite continuous and convex. The primary functions max(g,-N) have the extension above, and infimum commutes with max at a fixed cutoff, giving the all-semivaluation extension g=-v(z_1). Along monomial weights (t,1,...,1), g=-t; at support (z_1) it is minus infinity. Thus this member lies outside the bounded uniform class. Defining a decreasing completion alone does not prove an appropriate singular formal class or general conductor compatibility.

Remaining gates are an unbounded class with positivity and regularity on arbitrary excellent germs; complete smooth BFJ recovery; exact cone descent across general conductor support; and further analytic boundary-trace comparison. The numerical curve class already differs from the stipulated radial disc class on mixed-zero faces. No arbitrary-model cofinality or larger nonnormal Weil-effective convention is silently asserted. P12.3–P12.6 remain unproved. There is no priority claim, self-acceptance or external catalogue mutation.

Deliverables are P12.2-paper.tex, build/P12.2-paper.pdf, argument.md, native-notes.json, original-scope-decision.md, source-application-ledger.md, scope-and-gaps.md, whole-proof-coverage.md, input-hashes.json, own-hashes.json, environment.json, commands.md, README.md and build-report.md. The final paper has 14 pages and the final build reports no warnings or overfull boxes. The first 13-page build's 22.96107pt overfull box and outline warning are retained in build/pass1.stdout and build/pass1.log, with its PDF preserved. A failed own patch verification is retained in evidence/edit-report.md and was corrected without changing frozen inputs. Seven exact node arithmetic checks and the source-sign example passed; they are finite diagnostics, not mathematical certification. Notes have valid earlier local supports, and 44 own artifacts are hashed.
